chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: Okay, let's recap what we've learned about Q-Learning.

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: First, let's consider what it takes to build a model.

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: First step is define states, actions, and rewards.

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: So states are combinations of our features.

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: Actions are buy, sell, do nothing.

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: And rewards are some type of return.

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: Next, you choose the training period.

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: And you iterate over that training period and

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: update your Q-Table on each iteration.

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: When you reach the end of that training period,

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: you backtest to see how good the model is.

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: And you go back and

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: repeat until the model quits getting better.

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: Once it's converged, you stop, you've got your model.

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: Testing the model is simple.

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: You just backtest it on later data.

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: Remember, we're always training on one set of data and

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: then testing on later data.

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: And that's it.

chunks.title: Q Learning Recap
chunks.text: I hope you enjoyed the lesson.

text: Okay, let's recap what we've learned about Q-Learning. First, let's consider what it takes to build a model. First step is define states, actions, and rewards. So states are combinations of our features. Actions are buy, sell, do nothing. And rewards are some type of return. Next, you choose the training period. And you iterate over that training period and update your Q-Table on each iteration. When you reach the end of that training period, you backtest to see how good the model is. And you go back and repeat until the model quits getting better. Once it's converged, you stop, you've got your model. Testing the model is simple. You just backtest it on later data. Remember, we're always training on one set of data and then testing on later data. And that's it. I hope you enjoyed the lesson.
